# Data Viz Gotchas

> Known data-visualization and chart-rendering patterns that cause silent failures or hard-to-debug errors.

## Entries

- [One normalization divisor across mixed-scale metrics silently clamps the chart](mixed-scale-divisor.md): Sharing one divisor / normalization constant across metrics on different scales (0..100 scores vs a 1..3 multiplier) clamps the larger-scale ones to a full bar and shrinks the smaller ones toward empty; the chart ships looking fine but conveys nothing. Map each metric's own domain to [0,1] instead of dividing every series by the same number. HIGH.
- [A sparkline with preserveAspectRatio="none" stretches its point markers into ellipses](sparkline-preserveaspectratio-none-stretches-markers.md): independent x/y scaling distorts circles; draw markers as positioned HTML at percentage coordinates. LOW.
- [elkjs costs ~480 KB gzipped; a pure tree only needs d3-hierarchy](elkjs-bundle-size-use-d3-hierarchy-for-trees.md): ELK's bundled build dwarfs the rest of a chart chunk; for a family tree (one parent per node) d3-hierarchy's tidy tree gives the same layout in ~5 KB. MEDIUM.
- [A tidy tree with wide fan-out becomes an unreadable strip](tidy-tree-wide-fanout-needs-comb-lanes.md): A family tree where most nodes are leaves (81 of 92 here) lays out ~10,000 px wide and 5 levels deep, so fit-to-view needs ~15% zoom; stack each parent's childless children into balanced 'comb' lanes and route edges down a spine beside each lane. MEDIUM.
